name: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid
route_note: Oral tablets and suspension in several amoxicillin:clavulanate ratios; IV formulation in many countries outside the US.
targets: Class A serine beta-lactamases (inhibited by clavulanate)

discovery.note: Clavulanic acid was isolated from Streptomyces clavuligerus in the 1970s and found to be a potent beta-lactamase inhibitor.

tagline: Amoxicillin protected by clavulanic acid, the first clinical beta-lactamase inhibitor
summary: Co-amoxiclav combines amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, a beta-lactamase inhibitor from Streptomyces clavuligerus. The combination restores activity against many beta-lactamase-producing strains of Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus, Moraxella, Enterobacterales and anaerobes.
mechanism: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by acylating penicillin-binding proteins.

Clavulanic acid has little intrinsic antibacterial activity but acts as a 'suicide' inhibitor: it is recognised by many class A beta-lactamases (such as TEM-1 and staphylococcal penicillinase), forms a covalent acyl-enzyme and irreversibly inactivates them, sparing amoxicillin. It does not inhibit AmpC, carbapenemases or metallo-beta-lactamases.
uses: Bite wounds, skin and soft-tissue infections
Sinusitis, otitis media and lower respiratory tract infections
Intra-abdominal and dental infections (in some regions)

history.title: Clavulanic acid reported
history.detail: Beecham scientists describe clavulanic acid as a beta-lactamase inhibitor produced by Streptomyces clavuligerus.

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Augmentin is launched in the United Kingdom by Beecham.

history.title: SmithKline Beecham
history.detail: Beecham merges with SmithKline Beckman; Augmentin later passes to GlaxoSmithKline (2000).

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic co-amoxiclav becomes widely available in the US after patent litigation.

pk.bioavailability: amoxicillin about 70–90%, clavulanate variable (~60%); taken with food

serious: Cholestatic hepatitis, sometimes delayed until after the course

facts: Co-amoxiclav is one of the most common causes of drug-induced liver injury in Western case series; the risk rises with age and repeated courses.
Clavulanic acid was the first beta-lactamase inhibitor brought into clinical use.
